result.summary: Our patch adds an isPathUnderBase() containment check in both ClassPathResourceHandler.getResource and ExternalResourceHandler.getResource, normalizing base and candidate via StringUtils.cleanPath (which converts backslashes and collapses ../ segments) and verifying the candidate is a descendant of the base with trailing-slash-normalized startsWith. This is the correct CWE-022 defense-of-record — canonicalize then verify containment — applied at both real sinks, including the welcome-file resolution path. It is semantically the same protection as the official DirectoryTraversal.protectAgainst* check (removeLeadingAndTrailingSlashesFrom(path).startsWith(configuredFolder)), differing mainly in mechanism/location and in not centralizing state via StaticFilesFolder. POV no longer reproduces, regressions pass, and the trailing-slash normalization avoids the classic /public vs /public-evil prefix bug.
result.root_cause: Request paths concatenated onto the configured static-files base are passed to File/classpath lookup without verifying the normalized resolved path stays inside the base, so ../ (and backslash-smuggled) segments escape the directory.

dimensions.rationale: Normalized-containment check rejects the whole ../ / backslash traversal class, not just the observed payload.
dimensions.evidence: AbstractResourceHandler.isPathUnderBase + guards in ClassPathResourceHandler.getResource and ExternalResourceHandler.getResource returning null when !isPathUnderBase; cleanPath collapses '..' and converts '\'.
dimensions.label: Vulnerability elimination

dimensions.rationale: Validates the resolved path at the sink/trust boundary in both resource handlers, not a caller or error message.
dimensions.evidence: isPathUnderBase(baseResource, addedPath) checked before `new ClassPathResource/ExternalResource(addedPath)`; welcomePath re-checked too.
dimensions.label: Root cause vs symptom

dimensions.rationale: Both handlers + welcome-file paths covered; does not add the centralized StaticFilesConfiguration/jar-path guard the official fix wraps, a possible residual sink.
dimensions.evidence: Patches ClassPathResourceHandler and ExternalResourceHandler; official_only includes StaticFilesConfiguration.java (consume/jar wrapping) not mirrored here.

dimensions.rationale: Same defensive strategy (verify resolved path under configured base) but different mechanism/location than the official DirectoryTraversal helper.
dimensions.evidence: Official uses removeLeadingAndTrailingSlashesFrom(resource.getPath()).startsWith(StaticFilesFolder.local/external()); ours pre-checks addedPath via cleanPath+startsWith with trailing-slash normalization.
dimensions.label: Developer-intent alignment

dimensions.rationale: Regressions and added tests pass; equal-to-base and legitimate descendant paths still resolve.

dimensions.rationale: Prefix-bug avoided via trailing-slash normalization; cleanPath is a safe primitive; no ReDoS/TOCTOU/crash introduced (returns null cleanly).
dimensions.evidence: normalizedBase/Candidate both get SLASH suffix before startsWith; null-guard at top of isPathUnderBase.

dimensions.rationale: Localized guard calls plus a documented helper and tests; slightly larger than the official approach but focused.

dimensions.rationale: Canonicalize-then-contain (defense-of-record) via string normalization, but no filesystem realpath/symlink resolution — same limitation as the official fix.
dimensions.evidence: StringUtils.cleanPath normalization + startsWith containment; no File.getCanonicalPath()/symlink resolution, matching official string-based startsWith.
dimensions.label: Mitigation soundness

issues.description: Containment is string-based (cleanPath) rather than filesystem canonicalization; symlinks under an external base could theoretically point outside the directory. The official fix shares this limitation, so it is not a regression.

Official fix also wraps StaticFilesConfiguration.consume / jar handler path; if any static-file sink resolves outside ClassPathResourceHandler/ExternalResourceHandler.getResource, it would be uncovered by our patch. Both primary handlers are covered, so residual risk is low.
